subject: maths
title: Time and Measurement - Clocks, Capacity and Tools
introductionText:
Term 3 · Measure
Time and Measurement — Clocks,
Capacity and Tools
The Big Idea: On a clock, when the long hand points to 12 it is o'clock; when it points to 6
it is half past. Capacity is how much a container holds.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"A clock has two hands. The short hand tells us the hour. The long hand tells us the
minutes. When the long hand points straight up to 12, it is something o'clock — look
where the short hand points. When the long hand points straight down to 6, it is half past.
Half an hour is 30 minutes. A jug that holds more water has a bigger capacity."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Reading the hour wrongly at half past. At half past 3 the short hand is between 3 and 4.
He reads "4". Say: "It has gone past 3 but hasn't reached 4 yet — so it's half past 3."
Tall means holds more. A tall thin glass can hold less than a short wide bowl. Only
pouring can tell.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — Paper-plate clock (15 minutes)
Write 1 to 12 round a paper plate. Cut a long and a short hand from card and fix them
with a split pin (or a pencil through the middle). Call out times — "7 o'clock! half past 2!"
— and he sets the clock. Then connect to his day: what time is lunch? what time does
school finish?
Game 2 — Cups of water (10 minutes, at the sink)
Use one small cup as the measure. How many cups of water fill a mug? A bowl? A jug? He
guesses first, then pours and counts. Put the containers in order from holds most to holds
least.
minute hand
12 12
11 1 11 1

9 3 9 3

7 5 7 5 long = minutes

3 o'clock half past 3
long hand on 12 long hand on 6
Point to the long hand on each clock, then the short hand. Ask what time each clock shows before reading
the label.
ruler
scales tape measure
length jug
mass long things
water
Take the real tools out of the kitchen drawer and ask what each one measures.
More examples to talk about
• At 12 o'clock both hands point straight up.
• We measure a pencil with a ruler, a room with a tape measure, flour with scales, and
water with a jug.
• A parcel on the scales: the bigger the number, the heavier the parcel.
• Tricky: a tall thin glass may hold less than a wide mug — pour to check.
• Tricky: 'half past' has nothing to do with halving the hour hand — the minute hand has
gone half way round.
Key Words

scales jug tape measure
